chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him about the Sa'ee (brisk walking) between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa. He said: When you reach the house that is on your right at the beginning of the valley, so briskly walk (sa') until you reach the first alleyway on your right after you have crossed the valley towards Al-Marwa. So when you reach it, stop the brisk walking and walk normally.

And when you come from Al-Marwa, begin from the alleyway which I described to you. So when you reach the door that is facing Al-Safa after you have crossed the valley, stop the brisk walking and walk normally.
For indeed, the brisk walking (Sa') is upon the men, and the brisk walking is not upon the women.

key_terms.السَّعْي: Brisk walking or sprinting during the ritual of Sa'ee
key_terms.الصَّفَا: Al-Safa, one of the two hills between which Sa'ee is performed
key_terms.الْمَرْوَة: Al-Marwa, the second of the two hills
key_terms.الْوَادِي: The valley, referring to the area between the two hills where brisk walking occurs

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between men and women in the ritual of Sa'ee between Safa and Marwa?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the specific geographical boundaries for the brisk walking (Sa') between Al-Safa and Al-Marwa, identifying the 'Qarn' (valley) markers where men must transition from walking to Sa' and vice versa. It highlights a key jurisprudential distinction in Shia fiqh where the ritual intensity of Sa' is obligatory for men but not for women, reflecting the principle of ease (rukhas) in religious obligations. The narration underscores the importance of precise ritual performance based on physical location within the Haram precincts.
